deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 20-23): pi is the fundamental group of the sphere minus three points 0, 1, infinity. It is free on the loops l_0, l_1, l_inf, which satisfy one relation, l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1. Gamma = Gamma_{0,3} = S_3 x Z/2 is the extended mapping class group of the 3-pointed sphere: S_3 permutes the points and the Z/2 is orientation reversal, i.e. complex conjugation. Sigma is the extension 1 -> pi -> Sigma -> Gamma -> 1, which can be read as the group of homotopy classes of homeomorphisms that move a base point. The previous page built a canonical lift of S_3 into Sigma, using the elements fixing a chosen base point P.

This page, first part. Take the Z/2 generated by the orientation-reversing element tau and let Sigma_tau be its preimage in Sigma; it is an index-2 extension of Z/2 by pi. Grothendieck identifies Sigma_tau with the 'cartographic group' of Malgoire(-Voisin), here in its bicoloured / pre-dessin form. Its generators are three involutions tau_0, tau_1, tau_inf, the reflections in the sides of the two triangles cut out by the real line. The defining relations (16) are just tau_i^2 = 1, so Sigma_tau is the free product Z/2 * Z/2 * Z/2. The map tau_i -> -1 to {+-1} has kernel pi, which is free on the 'rotations' l_0 = tau_inf tau_1, l_1 = tau_0 tau_inf, l_inf = tau_1 tau_0. One checks directly that l_inf l_1 l_0 = tau_1 tau_0 tau_0 tau_inf tau_inf tau_1 = 1. So the reflection (non-oriented) picture contains the oriented one: pi is the orientation-preserving subgroup.

Second part. He moves to a 'more synthetic' profinite description of the outer actions:
- Sigma^ is the profinite completion of Sigma, an extension of Gamma_{0,3} by pi^.
- Sigma^^ is the group of 'lacet' automorphisms of pi^: those sending each loop l_i to a conjugate of a power l_j^p (inertia-preserving), with a common multiplier p in Z^*, as made explicit on the next page.
- This gives (18): 1 -> pi^ -> Sigma^^ -> Gamma^^ = Autext_lac(pi^) -> 1. It contains Sigma^ as a sub-extension.

The following page then takes the commutant of S_3 in Gamma^^ (a GT-type group containing the image of Gal(Qbar/Q) and complex conjugation). It asks whether S_3 x (commutant) exhausts Gamma^^, and parametrizes elements by (p, g_0, g_1, g_inf) with u(l_i) = int(g_i^{-1}) l_i^p. This is a precursor of the Drinfeld/Ihara description of GT^ and of inertia-preserving outer automorphism groups.
errors: The machine transcription writes Gamma_{0,3} = S_3 x Z/12 and 'image inverse de Z/12'. The previous page and the mathematics (orientation reversal) require Z/2. The manuscript most likely reads Z/2, possibly with a small mark that was misread.

No mathematical errors on the page. The kernel of Z/2*Z/2*Z/2 -> {+-1} is indeed free of rank 2 (rational Euler characteristic -1/2, index 2, giving -1). The relation l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1 holds. The relations (17) begin with crossed-out false starts, which is fine.

ideas.what: Preimage of the orientation-reversal Z/2 in the extension of Gamma_{0,3} by pi, identified with the free product of three involutions tau_i, with pi as the orientation-preserving kernel and l_0 = tau_inf tau_1 etc.
ideas.modern_name: Cartographic group / extended (reflection) triangle group (2,2,2-free) for hypermaps; non-oriented dessins
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malgoire & Voisin (cartographic groups, 1970s); Jones-Singerman (maps and hypermaps); Grothendieck in Esquisse d'un programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of cartographic groups C_2 and of oriented vs non-oriented maps

ideas.what: Profinite completion of the extension of Gamma_{0,3} = S_3 x Z/2 by pi^, embedded in the extension of Autext_lac(pi^) (inertia-preserving outer automorphisms) by pi^
ideas.modern_name: Inertia-preserving outer automorphism group Out_I(F^_2) / Out^C(Pi_{0,3}); ambient group for GT^ with complex conjugation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s), Nakamura; Hoshi-Mochizuki for Out^C
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, Gal(Qbar/Q) acting on pi_1 of P^1 minus 3 points), in general terms only

missed.claim: Grothendieck works from the start with the extended mapping class group S_3 x Z/2, including orientation reversal / complex conjugation. He realizes the conjugation part via the reflection (cartographic) group. He then embeds everything in the extension of Autext_lac(pi^) by pi^. In published GT literature, complex conjugation is usually treated as an add-on element of GT^ rather than through this reflection-group framework. This is a matter of presentation and is largely known in substance.
missed.quote: Le sous-groupe Sigma_tau ... est le groupe cartographique ... de Malgoire ... Sigma_tau peut être considéré comme le groupe gén. les tau_i, avec les seules relations (16)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that the 1981 drafts already set up the profinite GT-type object together with orientation reversal, three years before the Esquisse. It is mainly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains standard facts (the free product of three Z/2 has a free orientation-preserving subgroup of rank 2) and the setup of the profinite inertia-preserving outer automorphism extension. This is an early but recognisable form of ideas later made public in the Esquisse and in Drinfeld/Ihara's GT. It is historically nice but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Z/12' should read 'Z/2', in both 'image inverse de Z/2 engendré par tau' and 'Gamma_{0,3} = S_3 x Z/2'.
The tilde/'10' mark over Sigma in the first line is probably a marginal annotation, not part of the notation; the group is Sigma.
'les involutions[?] tau_i -> -1' is better read as 'l'homomorphisme tau_i -> -1 de Sigma_tau dans ±1'.
'bi-coloré[?] prédiré[?]' is uncertain; it plausibly refers to the bicoloured (hypermap / pre-dessin) variant of Malgoire's cartographic group.
'actions extérieures à droite[?]' is likely 'actions extérieures' or 'automorphismes lacets'.
In (18) the transcription writes the Gamma-hat with a double hat; the image shows the same object later called Gamma^! on the next page.
